We went because my dog ​​had an eye problem (she's an older dog). They diagnosed her with glaucoma, cataracts, and an ulcer. They prescribed a long list of medications, but there was no improvement. My dog ​​continued to have discomfort, and a small spot (like mucus) appeared in her eye.
I had to take her to an ophthalmologist. There, they measured her eye pressure (something they didn't do at the vet), performed an ultrasound, and gave her a thorough examination. They told us there was neither glaucoma nor cataracts. She had a poorly treated corneal ulcer, which was already showing signs of infection. They prescribed other medications, and she has gradually improved.
I don't doubt the doctors' abilities, but unfortunately, they only scared us and didn't help my dog. We were unlucky because they had been recommended to us. But it left us with a bad experience.
